text:
marta: Heads up — eval run `bench/v2/synthetic-cohorts` shows unexpectedly high overlap between holdout and train prompts. Looks like ~12% identical prompts across splits.
cheng: whoa, that's huge. any idea where they came from?
marta: synthetic generator pipeline uses seeded augmentation. I suspect we reused the same seed when generating cohort variants for A/B.
sam: can you paste the sampling call?
marta: snippet: `python synth_gen.py --seed 42 --cohort alpha --augment 3` then `--cohort beta --seed 42 --augment 3` — obvious mistake.
eva: that would deterministically produce identical variants for alpha/beta. we've hit this before but forgottento add split salt.
ci-bot: CI: bench/v2/synthetic-cohorts failed — leak-check metric exceeded threshold (leak_fraction=0.12 > 0.01). See artifacts: s3://redwood-evals/artifacts/1859876543/leak-report.json
qa: leak-report shows matching prompt fingerprints across cohorts, plus two fixtures where prompt templates collapsed to same string after post-processing.
cheng: quick fix: add cohort_id into RNG seed derivation. e.g. `seed = hash(seed || cohort_id || run_id)` so each cohort unique.
sam: +1. also we should add prompt-fingerprint unit test in eval-harness. test should regen two cohorts with same nominal seed and assert zero exact-match overlap.
marta: agree. I'll open a small PR: `eval-harness: add cohort-salt to seed and add test`.
eva: also consider making the default synth pipeline include a `--salt` param and failing the job if salt is not provided for multi-cohort runs. Adds a safety net.
cheng: aside — runner currently dedupes on trimmed text only. We should compute canonical fingerprint: normalized whitespace, lowercasing, stable tokenization id, and then sha256. Sample code: ```
def fingerprint(s):
    s2 = re.sub(r"\\s+", " ", s.strip()).lower()
    toks = tokenizer.encode(s2)
    return sha256(toks.tobytes()).hexdigest()
```
sam: that change will help avoid collisions from punctuation/noise. but be careful with tokenization non-determinism across tokenizer versions. we should include tokenizer-version metadata in the fingerprint input.
qa: good point — the leak-report already flagged 2 cases where tokenizer v1 vs v2 encoded differently and caused false negatives.
marta: for CI: propose a new quick-check job `leak-sanity` that runs fast: regen minimal cohorts, compute fingerprint overlap, and fail if overlap > 0%. Add it to eval CI matrix for any PR touching `synth_gen.py` or `eval-harness/runner`.
eva: also add a dashboard alert in Redwood Console: `evals/leakage-regressions` that surfaces leak_fraction by commit.
cheng: implementation plan: (1) change seed derivation + add `--salt`, (2) implement canonical fingerprint + include tokenizer-version, (3) add unit test and fast CI job, (4) update leak-report to include sample hashes and file offsets.
sam: timeline?
marta: I'll do (1) and (3) today (small PR). cheng will take (2) tomorrow. evawill wire CI job and dashboard after merges.
eva: noted. I'll create the `leak-sanity` job in CI and the Console tile — putting on my queue for today.
ci-bot: Note: creating ephemeral artifact bucket for reproducer: s3://redwood-evals/temp/1859876543-repro.zip
qa: after fixes, we should re-run the full bench/v2 run on a dedicated shard (not shared CI) to confirm leak_fraction < 0.01 and also run the quantized runner to ensure no accidental cache sharing introduced by the salt change.
cheng: one more thing — alert about metric definitions: currently leak_fraction = exact_match_count / total_holdout. We should also report near-duplicates by edit-distance and token-overlap as secondary fields so we can catch paraphrase-level leakage.
sam: fine. add `near_dup_rate` and `avg_jaccard` to report JSON.
marta: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/eval-harness/pull/812 — includes seed salt and test. Asking for review @cheng @eva @sam.
eva: reviewing now. thanks.
cheng: LGTM on the seed change, left a comment re: tokenizer-version integration.
sam: will help add CI job once PR is merged.
qa: follow-up: let's add an automation that runs the leak-sanity check against any synthetic dataset generation job on schedule (daily) so we get early warning beyond PRs.
marta: agreed. setting up a daily scheduled workflow.
ci-bot: CI: re-run requested by marta for bench/v2/synthetic-cohorts (triggered).
qa: thanks — keeping an eye on the re-run results.
